T1059.001.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1059.001.triage: Decode any -enc payload. Malicious use usually has an Office or script-host parent, hidden windows, execution-policy bypass, or a download cradle. IT automation runs from known script paths under SCCM or explorer.exe.

T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.triage: Compare the failure count with the user's baseline and check the source IP. Dozens to hundreds of failures from an external address, especially across several accounts, indicate guessing or spraying. A handful of internal failures is usually a mistyped or expired password.

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.triage: A successful sign-in from a new country or an impossible-travel pair is high risk when preceded by failures or tied to a privileged account. Check VPN egress and travel records before escalating.

T1003.001.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
T1003.001.triage: comsvcs.dll MiniDump, procdump -ma lsass, or taskmgr dumps of lsass are credential theft until proven otherwise. Defender scans and WerFault crash handling also touch LSASS and are benign.

T1048.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
T1048.triage: rclone, curl uploads, or password-protected archives sent to external hosts suggest exfiltration. Nightly backups to internal backup servers and OneDrive sync are normal even at high volume.

T1021.002.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
T1021.002.triage: PsExec or WMIC fanning out to many hosts from a user workstation is lateral movement. Patch deployments from IT run under services.exe or SCCM and touch fewer hosts per minute.

T1490.name: Inhibit System Recovery
T1490.triage: Deleting shadow copies or disabling recovery is a common last step before ransomware encryption; isolate quickly. Listing or creating shadow copies is routine backup activity.

T1053.005.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
T1053.005.triage: Tasks that run every few minutes, launch encoded PowerShell, or point at binaries in Public or Temp folders are persistence. Daily tasks pointing at IT script paths are usually maintenance.
